title: I Ran out of Titles.
reviewNotes: All 67 images and captions re-reviewed. The complete eight-piece fork position after ...Kc7 is reconstructed across the 76–77 second Nd8/Kb7/Qf7 to Nf7/Kc7 transition. Nxf7 is a legal winning witness to a seven-piece exact Black loss. Two branches check the queen capture and an independent d3/Ne5 continuation with all pawns preserved. Earlier nine-piece double offers and Arabian mate remain outside scope.
transcript: White's brilliant idea is rook to b8, sacrificing the rook completely. But of course, if the king takes the rook, now white is going to promote to [music] a queen and actually have the upper hand, having an extra knight and the checks. But black is not that naive, and instead he plays queen to d5 check, now attacking the white king and the knight at the same time. Now, after the king moves, the best option for black would actually be to take this knight, allow the promotion of the queen, and try to be extremely precise with the checks and make a repetition of moves, securing a draw. But who would ever do that when you can just pick up this pawn, make sure that no queen is ever going to be reborn, and the queen is going to be enough to fight off the rook and the knight. But actually, if black does take this pawn, this is now over and white is completely winning after rook to b7 followed [music] by the incredible, majestic, and brilliant knight to c6. A move that looks like a mouse slip, it does not even begin to make sense. [music] Both the rook and the knight are hanging, and yet neither of them can be captured. Of course, if you take the knight, the queen is [music] going to fall like this, and now a rook is going to be well enough to win the game. And if the black king takes the rook, now there is going to be knight to d8 with a fork, picking up the queen. And you have to be a little bit careful, but the knight is enough to win this game. But chess is not checkers, and you're under no obligation of capturing either of these pieces. So, black can create his own threat with queen to f4, now attacking the pawn and trying to go for a perpetual check. But unfortunately, this fails to rook to a7 with an Arabian [music] checkmate. If you love mind-blowing chess, follow for more.
